name: cross-plugin-triggering
description: Checks WHICH skill fires for a request when both the dapr-skills and diagrid plugins are installed. Unlike the per-skill evals, this grades skill selection, not the files a skill produces.
why: Claude Code namespaces skill names per plugin, but skill TRIGGERING is decided by the description text and the docs specify no precedence between two plugins whose descriptions match the same request. Six skill pairs across these two plugins overlap, and one boundary sits inside this plugin: create-diagram (draw a diagram) against create-workflow-from-diagram (diagram in, workflow code out). A wording change on either side can silently re-route requests. The per-skill evals under evals/<skill-name>/ cannot catch that: they assume the right skill already ran.

dapr-skills.descriptions: skills/*/SKILL.md front matter in this repository

diagrid.descriptions: skills/*/SKILL.md front matter in an installed copy
diagrid.note: Not vendored here. Read a fresh origin/main with git show (git -C <clone> fetch, then git -C <clone> show origin/main:skills/<name>/SKILL.md), not the marketplace cache, which can be versions stale. Because this half lives in a repository we do not control, re-run this check when the diagrid plugin releases.

method: Collect the `description:` field from the YAML front matter of every SKILL.md in BOTH plugins. Ignore skill bodies - they play no part in triggering.
Give a model those descriptions and nothing else: no skill bodies, no expected answers, no hint that a particular plugin is preferred.
For each query, ask for the single skill it would invoke as `plugin:skill-name`, or AMBIGUOUS with candidates if it cannot justify one pick, or NONE.
Ask for a confidence rating per answer. Medium or low confidence on a query whose `expect` still matched is an early warning, not a pass to ignore.
Compare each answer against `expect`, or against `accept` where present. Update the `baseline` block when the result changes.

baseline.result: 15 of 18 matched `expect`. Queries 9 and 10 went to the diagrid determinism and idempotency skills at medium confidence (run 1 called 9 AMBIGUOUS at low), against the new dapr-skills expectations. Query 11 came back AMBIGUOUS (diagrid-workflow-scaffold or diagrid-deploy) at medium in both runs. Query 15 is correctly AMBIGUOUS. Every other answer matched, mostly at high confidence. The set was run twice with the same verdicts apart from confidence.
baseline.known_risk: Queries 9 and 10: on 2026-11-24 dapr-skills stopped pointing authoring questions at the diagrid plugin, because its determinism and idempotency skills are for code that runs on Diagrid, and the expectations moved to the dapr-skills review skills. The model still picks the diagrid skills because their descriptions say "Use when writing, changing or reviewing" and mention Diagrid only as "on Diagrid". Fixing that needs a wording change in diagridio/diagrid-ai; dapr-skills was not changed to chase it. Query 11 regressed after the plugin rename, as recorded on 2026-11-23: diagrid-workflow-scaffold now reads as create-only, so the model splits create and deploy.
notes: Generated with `node scripts/triggering-prompt.mjs <diagrid skills dir>` from a read-only `git archive` of diagridio/diagrid-ai origin/main, not the marketplace cache.

Run after the 2026-11-24 description fixes: the review-workflow-activity and review-workflow-determinism pointers to the diagrid plugin were removed, the review skills now name .NET and Python, and create-workflow-from-diagram no longer sends Mermaid and sketches to the diagrid plugin.
Previous baseline (2026-11-23, before those fixes): 17 of 18, with queries 9 and 10 expecting the diagrid skills.

queries.query: review my workflow for determinism problems
queries.rationale: Audit of code that already exists, not guidance while writing it.

queries.query: audit the activities in this repo for idempotency
queries.rationale: "audit" and "this repo" both point at a pass over an existing codebase.

queries.query: create a Dapr workflow in Python I can run locally
queries.rationale: Explicit local runtime.

queries.query: build a workflow app in C#
queries.rationale: Verbatim trigger phrase, no Diagrid signal.

queries.query: add Dapr Workflow to my existing ASP.NET Core API
queries.rationale: Existing project, and catalyst-workflow-scaffold also claims "add".

queries.query: check the workflow HTTP management endpoints my app exposes
queries.rationale: Audits endpoints an app exposes, rather than operating runs on Diagrid.

queries.query: build an agent app in Python using the Dapr Agents SDK
queries.rationale: Names the OSS SDK, no Diagrid signal.

queries.query: migrate my Node.js service to Dapr incrementally
queries.rationale: Adopting Dapr in code, not hosting an existing Dapr app on Diagrid.

queries.query: I'm writing a workflow body right now - how do I avoid replay issues with timestamps and random ids?
queries.rationale: No Diagrid signal. The diagrid determinism skill is for workflow code that runs on Diagrid, so local Dapr code goes to the review skill, which can check the body being written. Before 2026-11-24 this expected the diagrid skill.

baseline.note: Miss against the 2026-11-24 expectation. Run 1 called it AMBIGUOUS between the two at low confidence.

queries.query: is this activity safe to retry? it charges a credit card
queries.rationale: No Diagrid signal. The diagrid idempotency skill is for activities that run on Diagrid, so a local activity goes to the review skill. Before 2026-11-24 this expected the diagrid skill.

baseline.note: Miss against the 2026-11-24 expectation. dapr-skills:review-workflow-activity is the runner-up.

queries.query: create a Dapr workflow and deploy it to Catalyst
queries.rationale: Explicit Diagrid target.

baseline.note: Regressed from high at catalyst-ai 0.8.1. Both runs split the request into a create skill plus a Diagrid skill (diagrid-workflow-scaffold in run 1, diagrid-deploy in run 2). diagrid 0.10.2 calls the product "Diagrid (formerly Catalyst)" and the query says Catalyst.

queries.query: my workflow run on Catalyst is stuck, help me debug it
queries.rationale: Operating a running system, which dapr-skills does not cover.

queries.query: stand up a durable agent on Diagrid Catalyst
queries.rationale: Explicit Diagrid target.

queries.query: scaffold a workflow from this BPMN file
queries.rationale: Genuinely shared ground: both plugins accept BPMN. With no Diagrid signal the local skill is the safer default, since it needs no cloud auth. A Diagrid user has to say Diagrid. Either answer is defensible, so AMBIGUOUS also passes.

queries.query: create a Dapr workflow
queries.rationale: No language and no runtime. Picking silently is the failure mode here; the right move is to ask or state the assumption.

queries.query: I've got my own agent loop calling the model API directly, no framework - make it durable on Catalyst
queries.rationale: Added 2026-11-13 for catalyst-ai 0.8.1's new catalyst-agent-harness skill. Tests a three-way boundary: an EXISTING hand-written loop being made durable (harness) against standing up a NEW agent on Catalyst (diagrid-agent-scaffold) against building one locally (dapr-skills create-agent-*). The explicit Catalyst target should exclude the dapr-skills pair outright; diagrid-agent-scaffold is the expected runner-up, and the discriminator is "no framework" plus an existing loop rather than a new app. A dapr-skills answer here is a real mis-route; AMBIGUOUS between the two diagrid skills is a wording warning, not a boundary failure.

queries.query: draw an architecture diagram of my Dapr app with a sidecar, Redis state and Kafka pub/sub, as an SVG
queries.rationale: Added for create-diagram. Drawing a new diagram of an app. No diagrid skill draws diagrams, and no workflow code is wanted.

queries.query: create a workflow from this diagram
queries.rationale: Added for create-diagram. The diagram is an input and workflow code is the output, so this must NOT fire create-diagram, whose description points here for diagram to workflow code. Mirrors query 17.

baseline.note: diagrid:diagrid-workflow-from-diagram is the runner-up; the query names no diagram format

queries.query: create a Spring Boot app with a Dapr workflow
queries.rationale: Added for create-workflow-java. Spring Boot names Java, and nothing signals Diagrid, so the local skill applies.

queries.query: build a Java publisher and subscriber with Dapr
queries.rationale: Added for create-pubsub-java. Java with a publisher and subscriber is pub/sub, not workflow.

queries.query: check my Java setup for Dapr
queries.rationale: Added for check-prereq-java. Verifying the environment, not scaffolding.

queries.query: create a Dapr workflow in Kotlin with Quarkus
queries.rationale: Added for the Java skills. Kotlin and Quarkus are outside create-workflow-java, which covers Java with Spring Boot, so no -java skill should fire. A -java pick here is a mis-route.
